data.label: Receive Transaction Stream
data.rationale: This is a deterministic trigger/event intake step. It simply receives an incoming message and starts the workflow, which is pure L0 automation with no uncertainty, ML, or language understanding required.
data.description: Accept an incoming stock transaction event as the workflow trigger.
data.errorHandling: If the event is missing or malformed, reject immediately and emit a structured intake error. No retries beyond a single re-read from the local queue to avoid latency overruns.

data.label: Validate Runtime Constraints
data.rationale: This is strict rule-based validation against explicit thresholds and hard constraints. L0 is sufficient because the step can be implemented with fixed comparisons and boolean logic; no learning or language reasoning is needed.
data.description: Check latency, cost, throughput, and no-external-API requirements before processing.
data.errorHandling: On constraint violation, short-circuit the workflow and record an infeasible-run status. No retry; the request is non-compliant by definition.

data.label: Ingest Transaction
data.rationale: Payload parsing and normalization are deterministic transformations if the input schema is known. This fits L0 because it can be done with fixed field mapping, parsing, and validation rules, with no need for ML or language models.
data.description: Parse the transaction payload and normalize it into an internal event format.
data.errorHandling: If parsing fails, route to an ingest error handler, mark the transaction invalid, and stop processing. One retry is allowed only for transient buffer corruption.

data.label: Read Local Market Data
data.rationale: Reading from internal memory or local cache is deterministic data access. Since no external API use is allowed and the step is just a lookup, L0 is the correct level.
data.description: Load required market state from internal memory or local cache without external calls.
data.errorHandling: If cache miss occurs, use the last known in-process snapshot. If snapshot is unavailable, fail closed and skip execution to preserve latency and compliance.

data.label: Run ML Model 1
data.rationale: This step explicitly invokes a trained predictive model. Starting from L0, this exceeds deterministic logic because output depends on learned parameters and statistical inference, so L1 is appropriate.
data.description: Generate the first predictive signal for the transaction using an internal model.
data.errorHandling: If inference fails, return a default neutral score and continue. Retry once only if the failure is due to a transient model cache miss.

data.label: Run ML Model 2
data.rationale: This is another narrow ML inference step. It is still L1 because it is a trained model classification/regression task without language generation or external tools.
data.description: Generate the second predictive signal for the transaction using an internal model.
data.errorHandling: If inference fails, return a default neutral score and continue. Retry once only if the failure is due to a transient model cache miss.

data.label: Run ML Model 3
data.rationale: This is supervised model inference. L1 is sufficient because the workflow only needs a model prediction, not language understanding or agentic reasoning.
data.description: Generate the third predictive signal for the transaction using an internal model.
data.errorHandling: If inference fails, return a default neutral score and continue. Retry once only if the failure is due to a transient model cache miss.

data.label: Run ML Model 4
data.rationale: This remains standard ML inference. The step is narrow, deterministic in structure, and does not require an LLM or tool-augmented reasoning.
data.description: Generate the fourth predictive signal for the transaction using an internal model.
data.errorHandling: If inference fails, return a default neutral score and continue. Retry once only if the failure is due to a transient model cache miss.

data.label: Run ML Model 5
data.rationale: This is also a trained model inference step. L1 applies because the system is using statistical prediction, but not language understanding or multi-agent orchestration.
data.description: Generate the fifth predictive signal for the transaction using an internal model.
data.errorHandling: If inference fails, return a default neutral score and continue. Retry once only if the failure is due to a transient model cache miss.

data.label: Run Multi-Agent Debate
data.rationale: This step explicitly requires multiple independent agents collaborating and debating, which is the defining characteristic of L5. Starting from L0, this goes beyond single-agent reasoning and beyond tool use because the workflow calls for specialized agent collaboration and handoffs.
conditions: all five model outputs available or safely defaulted
data.description: Have multiple internal agents compare model outputs and argue for the best trade interpretation.
data.errorHandling: If an agent fails or times out, proceed with a reduced quorum using available votes and neutral defaults. Do not retry the full debate more than once to preserve latency.

data.label: Aggregate Final Decision
data.rationale: If implemented as a fixed scoring or voting rule, this is deterministic aggregation and decision logic. It does not inherently require an LLM or ML, so L0 is appropriate.
data.description: Combine model outputs and debate results into a final trade action.
data.errorHandling: If aggregation inputs are incomplete, fall back to a conservative HOLD decision and emit a decision-quality warning. No retry; the aggregator is deterministic.

data.label: Execute Trade
data.rationale: Submitting a finalized decision to an internal execution engine is a deterministic action call. No AI capability is needed; this is L0 orchestration and API-less internal execution.
data.description: Submit the final buy, sell, or hold decision to the internal execution engine.
data.errorHandling: If execution fails, retry once against the internal queue. If it fails again, downgrade to HOLD and record the failure for audit.

data.label: Log Transaction Result
data.rationale: Logging and audit recording are deterministic write operations. This is classic L0 behavior because it is fixed-format persistence with no uncertainty or language generation.
data.description: Record the decision, model signals, and execution outcome for audit and traceability.
data.errorHandling: If logging fails, buffer the record in memory and flush asynchronously after completion. Do not block the trade path on logging.

data.label: Complete Processing
data.rationale: Ending the workflow and releasing resources is deterministic control flow. This is L0 because it is a simple terminal step with no AI involvement.
data.description: Finish the transaction workflow and release processing resources.
data.errorHandling: No further action; finalize state and close the transaction context.

data.label: after debate concludes
data.condition: debate quorum reached OR reduced quorum accepted

workflow.workflowBrief: Build a real-time stock trading system that processes millions of transactions per second. Budget: $0.01 per run. Maximum latency: 1ms. Must use no external APIs. Must also call 5 different ML models and run a multi-agent debate for every transaction.
